abiram_48.name: Abiram
abiram_48.who: Firstborn son of Hiel of Bethel, who died when his father laid the foundation of rebuilt Jericho.
key: Joshua had declared that whoever rebuilt Jericho would lay its foundation at the cost of his firstborn (Joshua 6).
When Hiel laid Jericho's foundation in Ahab's day, it cost him his firstborn Abiram (1 Kings 16).
His death fulfilled the word the Lord spoke through Joshua son of Nun (1 Kings 16).

agee_110.name: Agee
agee_110.who: A Hararite, the father of Shammah, one of David's three chief mighty men.
key: Agee the Hararite is named as the father of Shammah among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
His son Shammah held a field of lentils and struck down the Philistines (2 Samuel 23).

ammihud_226.name: Ammihud
ammihud_226.who: Father of Talmai, the king of Geshur with whom Absalom took refuge.
key: After killing Amnon, Absalom fled to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur (2 Samuel 13).
Absalom stayed in Geshur with Ammihud's son for three years (2 Samuel 13).

amorite_237.name: Amorites
amorite_237.who: A people descended from Canaan who held much of the land, west and east of the Jordan, before Israel's conquest.
key: The Amorites are listed among the descendants of Canaan son of Ham (Genesis 10).
God told Abram the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet complete (Genesis 15).
Israel defeated Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan east of the Jordan (Numbers 21).
Joshua defeated five Amorite kings who attacked Gibeon, as the sun stood still (Joshua 10).
Through Amos, God recalled destroying the Amorites, though they were tall as cedars (Amos 2).
amorite_237.label: People group

antipas_270.name: Antipas
antipas_270.who: A faithful witness of Christ who was put to death in Pergamum, where Satan dwells.
key: The risen Christ called Antipas my faithful witness (Revelation 2).
He was killed among the believers in Pergamum, where Satan's throne is (Revelation 2).
The church there held fast to Christ's name even in the days of Antipas (Revelation 2).

armoni_309.name: Armoni
armoni_309.who: A son of King Saul by his concubine Rizpah, handed over to the Gibeonites and put to death.
key: Armoni and his brother Mephibosheth were sons whom Rizpah bore to Saul (2 Samuel 21).
David gave them and five of Saul's grandsons to the Gibeonites, who hanged them (2 Samuel 21).
Rizpah guarded their bodies from birds and beasts until the rain came (2 Samuel 21).

asiel_344.name: Asiel
asiel_344.who: A man of the tribe of Simeon, father of Seraiah and ancestor of the clan chief Jehu.
key: Asiel is named in Simeon's genealogy as the father of Seraiah and forefather of Jehu (1 Chronicles 4).
His descendants were among the Simeonite princes whose clans increased greatly (1 Chronicles 4).

azrikam_563.name: Azrikam
azrikam_563.who: A descendant of David in the royal line after the exile, a son of Neariah.
key: Azrikam is listed with Elioenai and Hizkiah as the sons of Neariah (1 Chronicles 3).
His family belongs to David's royal line traced on through Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3).

beerah_431.name: Beerah
beerah_431.who: A Reubenite chief, son of Baal, carried into exile by Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria.
key: Beerah son of Baal is named in the line of Joel in the tribe of Reuben (1 Chronicles 5).
He was a chief of the Reubenites (1 Chronicles 5).
Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria carried him away into exile (1 Chronicles 5).

bilhan_504.name: Bilhan
bilhan_504.who: A Benjaminite, son of Jediael, whose sons headed fathers' houses of mighty warriors.
key: Bilhan is listed as the son of Jediael in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7).
His sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7).
Their descendants numbered 17,200 mighty warriors ready for war (1 Chronicles 7).

bukki_523.name: Bukki
bukki_523.who: A priest descended from Aaron through Eleazar, listed in the high-priestly line and among Ezra's ancestors.
key: Bukki son of Abishua is named in the line of Eleazar son of Aaron (1 Chronicles 6).
He was the father of Uzzi in this priestly line (1 Chronicles 6).
Ezra's genealogy traces back through Bukki to Aaron the chief priest (Ezra 7).

col-hozeh_951.name: Col-hozeh
col-hozeh_951.who: Father of Shallun, who ruled the district of Mizpah and rebuilt the Fountain Gate under Nehemiah.
key: Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate (Nehemiah 3).
Col-hozeh's son also built the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden (Nehemiah 3).

delaiah_1003.name: Delaiah
delaiah_1003.who: Son of Mehetabel and father of Shemaiah, who tried to frighten Nehemiah into hiding in the temple.
key: Nehemiah went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel (Nehemiah 6).
Delaiah's son urged Nehemiah to hide in the temple, but Nehemiah saw he had been hired (Nehemiah 6).

elymas_403.name: Elymas
elymas_403.who: A Jewish magician and false prophet on Cyprus, struck blind for opposing the gospel before the proconsul.
key: Bar-Jesus, a Jewish false prophet and magician, was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus (Acts 13).
Elymas opposed Barnabas and Saul, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith (Acts 13).
Filled with the Spirit, Paul declared he would be blind for a time, and darkness fell on him (Acts 13).
Seeing what happened, the proconsul believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord (Acts 13).

eshcol_1218.name: Eshcol
eshcol_1218.who: An Amorite near Hebron, brother of Mamre and Aner, and an ally of Abram.
key: Eshcol and his brothers Mamre and Aner were allies of Abram (Genesis 14).
They went with Abram when he pursued the eastern kings to rescue Lot (Genesis 14).
Abram asked that Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre receive their share of the spoil (Genesis 14).

ezer_1240.name: Ezer
ezer_1240.who: A son of Ephraim, killed with his brother Elead by the men of Gath in a clash over livestock.
key: Ezer and Elead were killed by the native-born men of Gath in a livestock raid (1 Chronicles 7).
Their father Ephraim mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him (1 Chronicles 7).
Ephraim then fathered Beriah, named because disaster had come on his house (1 Chronicles 7).

gazez_1282.name: Gazez
gazez_1282.who: A son of Caleb son of Hezron by his concubine Ephah, in the genealogy of Judah.
key: Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).
His brother Haran also named a son Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).

hamutal_1368.name: Hamutal
hamutal_1368.who: Daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of King Josiah, and mother of Kings Jehoahaz and Zedekiah.
key: Jehoahaz's mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah (2 Kings 23).
Her son Jehoahaz reigned three months before Pharaoh Neco imprisoned him (2 Kings 23).
She was also the mother of Zedekiah, Judah's last king (2 Kings 24).
Jeremiah's book repeats her name in recounting Zedekiah's reign and Jerusalem's fall (Jeremiah 52).

harim_1417.name: Harim
harim_1417.who: Father of Malchijah, who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall and the Tower of the Ovens.
key: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub repaired a second section of the wall (Nehemiah 3).
Their work included the Tower of the Ovens (Nehemiah 3).

husham_1578.name: Husham
husham_1578.who: A man from the land of the Temanites who reigned as king of Edom before Israel had kings.
key: When Jobab died, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place (Genesis 36).
After Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian, reigned in his place (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name in the list of Edom's early kings (1 Chronicles 1).

ichabod_1589.name: Ichabod
ichabod_1589.who: Son of the priest Phinehas, named by his dying mother after the ark of God was captured.
key: His mother went into labor on hearing the ark was taken and Phinehas and Eli were dead (1 Samuel 4).
As she died, she named him Ichabod, saying the glory had departed from Israel (1 Samuel 4).
Ahijah son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, later served as priest with Saul (1 Samuel 14).

igal_1598.name: Igal
igal_1598.who: Son of Joseph of Issachar, one of the twelve spies Moses sent to explore Canaan.
key: Moses sent Igal son of Joseph to represent Issachar among the twelve spies (Numbers 13).
He was among the spies who brought back a bad report of the land (Numbers 13).
The men who spread the bad report died by plague before the Lord (Numbers 14).

ishbak_620.name: Ishbak
ishbak_620.who: A son of Abraham by Keturah, sent away eastward with his brothers.
key: Keturah bore Abraham Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to his concubines' sons and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).
Chronicles repeats Ishbak among the sons of Keturah (1 Chronicles 1).

jada_684.name: Jada
jada_684.who: A man of Judah in the line of Jerahmeel, son of Onam and father of Jether and Jonathan.
key: Jada and his brother Shammai are listed as the sons of Onam (1 Chronicles 2).
Jada's sons were Jether and Jonathan; Jether died without children (1 Chronicles 2).
Jonathan's sons Peleth and Zaza carried on the line of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).

jakeh_712.name: Jakeh
jakeh_712.who: The father of Agur, whose wise sayings are collected in the book of Proverbs.
key: Proverbs 30 opens with the words of Agur son of Jakeh (Proverbs 30).
Jakeh's son confesses his weariness and limited understanding before God (Proverbs 30).

jarah_782.name: Jarah
jarah_782.who: A descendant of King Saul through Jonathan, son of Ahaz, in the genealogy of Benjamin.
key: The first list of Saul's line calls him Jehoaddah son of Ahaz (1 Chronicles 8).
In the repeated genealogy, Ahaz fathered Jarah (1 Chronicles 9).
Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri (1 Chronicles 9).

joel_1649.name: Joel
joel_1649.who: A Reubenite whose descendants, including Baal and the exiled chief Beerah, are listed in Chronicles.
key: The sons of Joel are traced through Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, and Baal (1 Chronicles 5).
His descendant Beerah, a Reubenite chief, was exiled by Tiglath-pileser of Assyria (1 Chronicles 5).

joel_1653.name: Joel
joel_1653.who: Brother of Nathan, named among David's mighty men in Chronicles.
key: Joel the brother of Nathan is listed among the mighty men of David's army (1 Chronicles 11).
These warriors gave David strong support in his kingdom, with all Israel (1 Chronicles 11).

joiakim_1681.name: Joiakim
joiakim_1681.who: A high priest after the exile, son of Jeshua and father of Eliashib.
key: Jeshua fathered Joiakim, and Joiakim fathered Eliashib in the high-priestly line (Nehemiah 12).
In Joiakim's days the heads of the priestly fathers' houses were recorded (Nehemiah 12).
He served in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe (Nehemiah 12).

jokshan_1685.name: Jokshan
jokshan_1685.who: A son of Abraham by Keturah and the father of Sheba and Dedan.
key: Keturah bore Jokshan and five other sons to Abraham (Genesis 25).
Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan; Dedan's descendants included the Asshurim and Letushim (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to Keturah's sons and sent them away eastward (Genesis 25).

luke_1836.name: Luke
luke_1836.who: A beloved physician and companion of Paul, traditionally recognized as the author of Luke and Acts.
key: The Gospel traditionally ascribed to Luke opens as an orderly account for Theophilus (Luke 1).
Paul sent greetings from Luke the beloved physician to the Colossians (Colossians 4).
Paul named Luke among his fellow workers in his letter to Philemon (Philemon 1).
In his final imprisonment, Paul wrote that only Luke was with him (2 Timothy 4).

matthan_1968.name: Matthan
matthan_1968.who: Son of Eleazar and grandfather of Joseph, Mary's husband, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.
key: Matthew lists Matthan son of Eleazar in Jesus' royal line descended from David (Matthew 1).
Matthan fathered Jacob, the father of Joseph the husband of Mary (Matthew 1).

medan_1978.name: Medan
medan_1978.who: A son of Abraham by Keturah, sent away eastward with his brothers.
key: Keturah bore Abraham Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to his concubines' sons and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).
Chronicles repeats Medan among the sons of Keturah (1 Chronicles 1).

milcom_2084.name: Milcom
milcom_2084.who: The detestable god of the Ammonites, whose worship Solomon brought into Israel and Josiah later abolished.
key: In his old age Solomon went after Milcom, the abomination of the Ammonites (1 Kings 11).
God tore ten tribes from Solomon's house because they had worshiped Milcom and other gods (1 Kings 11).
Josiah defiled the high places Solomon had built east of Jerusalem for Milcom (2 Kings 23).
Zephaniah announced judgment on those who swear by the Lord and yet by Milcom (Zephaniah 1).
milcom_2084.label: False god

pahath-moab_2265.name: Pahath-moab
pahath-moab_2265.who: Ancestral head of a large family whose descendants returned from exile with Zerubbabel and with Ezra.
key: The sons of Pahath-moab, through Jeshua and Joab, numbered 2,812 among the returning exiles (Ezra 2).
Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah led two hundred men of this family back with Ezra (Ezra 8).
Some of his descendants were among those who had married foreign wives (Ezra 10).
Nehemiah's list counts the family through Jeshua and Joab at 2,818 (Nehemiah 7).

philip_2345.name: Philip
philip_2345.who: A brother of Herod Antipas and the husband of Herodias before Antipas took her as his wife.
key: Herod had imprisoned John because of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife (Matthew 14).
John had told Herod it was not lawful to have his brother's wife (Mark 6).
Luke records that John reproved Herod over Herodias, his brother's wife (Luke 3).

ram_2393.name: Ram
ram_2393.who: Ancestor of the family to which Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, Job's young counselor, belonged.
key: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, burned with anger at Job (Job 32).
This descendant of Ram spoke only after Job's three older friends had no answer (Job 32).

rehum_2414.name: Rehum
rehum_2414.who: A commander in the province Beyond the River who wrote to Artaxerxes against Jerusalem and halted its rebuilding.
key: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes (Ezra 4).
They warned that if the city were rebuilt, it would stop paying tribute (Ezra 4).
Artaxerxes replied to Rehum, ordering the work stopped until he decreed otherwise (Ezra 4).
Rehum and his associates hurried to Jerusalem and by force made the Jews stop (Ezra 4).

segub_2483.name: Segub
segub_2483.who: Youngest son of Hiel of Bethel, who died when his father set up the gates of rebuilt Jericho.
key: Joshua had declared that whoever rebuilt Jericho would set its gates at the cost of his youngest son (Joshua 6).
Hiel set up Jericho's gates at the cost of his youngest son Segub, in Ahab's day (1 Kings 16).
This fulfilled the word of the Lord spoken through Joshua son of Nun (1 Kings 16).

shammai_2542.name: Shammai
shammai_2542.who: A man of Judah in the line of Jerahmeel, son of Onam and father of Nadab and Abishur.
key: Shammai and his brother Jada are listed as the sons of Onam (1 Chronicles 2).
Shammai's sons were Nadab and Abishur (1 Chronicles 2).
Abishur's wife Abihail bore him Ahban and Molid (1 Chronicles 2).

shobach_2717.name: Shobach
shobach_2717.who: Commander of Hadadezer's Syrian army, killed when David defeated the Syrians at Helam.
key: Hadadezer brought out the Syrians beyond the Euphrates, with Shobach commanding his army (2 Samuel 10).
David crossed the Jordan and fought the Syrians at Helam (2 Samuel 10).
Shobach was wounded and died there, and the Syrians feared to help the Ammonites again (2 Samuel 10).
Chronicles calls him Shophach and records his death in the same battle (1 Chronicles 19).

shuah_2727.name: Shuah
shuah_2727.who: A son of Abraham by Keturah, sent away eastward with his brothers.
key: Keturah bore Abraham Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to his concubines' sons and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).
Chronicles repeats Shuah among the sons of Keturah (1 Chronicles 1).

tebah_2832.name: Tebah
tebah_2832.who: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his concubine Reumah.
key: Abraham was told that Nahor's concubine Reumah bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22).
These sons are listed after the eight sons Milcah bore to Nahor (Genesis 22).

zalaph_2981.name: Zalaph
zalaph_2981.who: Father of Hanun, who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
key: Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).
Zalaph's son worked alongside Hananiah son of Shelemiah in the rebuilding (Nehemiah 3).

ziphah_3092.name: Ziphah
ziphah_3092.who: A man of Judah, son of Jehallelel, listed in the tribe's genealogy.
key: Ziphah is named among the sons of Jehallelel, with Ziph, Tiria, and Asarel (1 Chronicles 4).
His family is recorded among the clans descended from Judah (1 Chronicles 4).
